# A0 print pack — Anycubic Chiron

Status: TEST FIXTURE ONLY. These prints validate geometry; they are not production crawler parts.

## Files generated by GitHub Actions
Source: `CAD/PX1_A0_SourceMatch.py`.

Print for A0.1:
- 2 x `PX1_A0_SideFixturePlate_*.stl`;
- 5 x `PX1_A0_Z50_m1_PA20_TEST.stl` for one-side test, or 10 x for both sides simultaneously.

The fixture preserves the real 50 mm pitch-centre spacing of the five Z50 stations. It deliberately uses 6001-2RS bench bearings and Ø12 temporary shafts instead of pretending to reproduce unresolved production shaft/seal details.

## Chiron setup — fixture plates
Preferred: PETG.
- nozzle: 0.4 mm;
- layer: 0.24–0.28 mm;
- walls: 5;
- top/bottom: >= 6 layers;
- infill: 40–50% grid/gyroid;
- print flat on the largest face;
- supports: off;
- brim: 6–8 mm if corner lift appears.

PLA is acceptable only for dry dimensional fitting. Do not use a PLA fixture for sustained motor/gear heating tests.

## Chiron setup — Z50 geometry gears
For first hand-turn/mesh validation:
- PETG is acceptable;
- layer: 0.16–0.20 mm;
- walls: >= 5;
- infill: 80–100%;
- print flat with gear axis vertical;
- elephant-foot compensation approximately 0.15–0.25 mm if the slicer supports it;
- no support.

For powered A0.1 use PA/nylon or a tough engineering filament if available. Printed gears are intentionally not used for the final full-load A0.3 torque qualification.

## Bench hardware
Per one five-gear fixture:
- 10 x 6001-2RS, 12x28x8;
- 5 x straight Ø12 mm shafts, nominal length 24–30 mm depending on chosen collars/retention;
- 5 x Z50 printed test gears;
- shaft collars/spacers as required to keep each gear centered between plates without axial preload;
- M5 bench fasteners for end mounting;
- optional M4 retainers around bearing pockets.

A practical first assembly uses removable shaft collars outside both plates. Do not press bearings axially against each other through the plastic plates.

## Inspection before power
1. Verify center-to-center: adjacent shaft axes = 50.0 mm nominal.
2. Bearings should seat without splitting the print. Light hand press is acceptable; heavy press fit is not.
3. All five gears must rotate through at least 20 output revolutions by hand in both directions.
4. Mark any periodic tight point with shaft position and gear pair.
5. Only after hand-turn PASS connect temporary low-speed drive.

## What the fixture can close
- real five-gear kinematic chain and direction;
- 50 mm centre spacing;
- practical backlash trend for the test PA20 profile;
- shaft/plate stiffness needed for A0;
- whether the source-like motor/bevel input can drive the complete five-gear train.

## What it cannot close
- OEM Proteus tooth correction/profile;
- production Z50 bore/hub;
- production bearing fits;
- seals and pressure body;
- final wheel retention;
- production gear material/heat treatment.
